name: IQ Puzzles — Level 13

description: 29 verbatim puzzles from Level 13, with official solutions.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which of the bottom boxes goes in the middle of this sequence?
questions.explanation: Reading from the left, line by line, the @ moves in a figure of 8 around the corners, the * moves anticlockwise in steps of 2 around the 2 central columns, and the △ moves to and fro along the third row.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the web?
questions.explanation: The numbers in the top half of the outer ring are written in reverse order plus 1 in the inner ring and vice versa.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which playing cards are needed to fill in the blanks?
questions.correctAnswer: From top to bottom, Jack of Hearts, Seven of Clubs, Queen of Clubs and Two of Diamonds.
questions.explanation: The grid displays rotational symmetry 180° around the central Ace of Hearts, with the cards swapping to the other suit of the same colour.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What is missing from the empty segment?
questions.explanation: In the top pair of boxes the letters are rotated 90° clockwise and the corresponding numerical value is put in the segments on the right. The bottom pair of boxes follows the same rule but the reverse numerical alphabetical value is put on the box on the left.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letters finish the grid?
questions.explanation: Starting at the top of the first 2 columns and working down, each pair of letters is duplicated in the right hand columns from the bottom up with each letter advancing one place alphabetically.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which two letters are missing from the bottom grids?
questions.explanation: Starting top left and working clockwise, move forward 6 places, back 2, then forward 4. etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the last circle?
questions.explanation: In each circle, multiply the top two numbers together to get a 2 digit number, add these together until you get a single figure number which goes in the bottom segment of each circle.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Complete the bottom grid.
questions.explanation: From top left digit add 2 to get the lower number. Add these together to get the next top number and continue for each column.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter goes at the bottom?
questions.explanation: Starting at the top, letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 places.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter goes in the empty square and completes the puzzle?
questions.explanation: Add the numerical value of the top left and centre letters to give the lower left letter, similarly with the top right and centre letters to give the lower right letter.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which domino fits into the empty space in this arrangement?
questions.explanation: The dots form a symmetrical pattern from top left to bottom right.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the wheel?
questions.explanation: Moving clockwise, double the previous number and add 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number completes the third triangle?
questions.explanation: In each triangle, multiply the bottom numbers to get a 2 digit number, add these together to get the top number.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What goes at the bottom of the last triangle?
questions.explanation: The number in the centre of each triangle equals the sum of the squares of the numerical values around each triangle.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the empty circle?
questions.explanation: The central value of 15 equals the average of the numbers on opposite sides of the diagram.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Fill in the correct number.
questions.explanation: The value in each lower box represents the sum of the squares of the two numbers directly above it.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes at the top of the third star?
questions.explanation: The sum of the left and right numbers equals the sum of the other three numbers.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is needed to complete this puzzle?
questions.explanation: In rows, the centre number equals the sum of the left and right hand numbers, plus the central number from above.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the empty box?
questions.explanation: In each row, multiply the first and second numbers, then subtract the third to give the value in the right hand box.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter replaces the blank and completes the sequence?
questions.explanation: Moving down the column, advance 2 letters, then back 5, etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the middle?
questions.explanation: Moving diagonally downwards from left to right, numbers increase by the same amount each line.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which watch is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Add all the digits on each watch together. All the others are square numbers.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What time should the blank clock show?
questions.correctAnswer: Any time whose two hands point to numbers adding to 10.
questions.explanation: The figures pointed to by the hands add up to 10, therefore a number of options are available.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter replaces the blank and completes the sequence?
questions.explanation: In rows, letters increase in numerical value by 3 as you move to the right.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter completes the wheel?
questions.explanation: Letters are arranged in pairs in opposite segments of the circle, the lower value letter is the same distance from the start of the alphabet as the other is from the end.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Fill in the empty segment.
questions.explanation: Take each letter in the left half of the circle and add 5, put the result in the opposite segment on the right.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter logically goes in the blank segment?
questions.explanation: In each circle, going clockwise, letters move back 3 places, then forward 1, etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Finish the chain by filling in the blank link.
questions.explanation: Going clockwise, add 1, then 2, then 3 etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Farmer Giles has sent his livestock to market for sale but the farmhand has forgotten how much he was to sell each animal for. The farmer though had drawn him some pictures which showed the equivalent value of each of the animals but didn’t finish it. Can you solve the problem for the luckless farmhand?
